Six divided by two, times one plus two in parentheses. Is the answer one or nine? The whole internet is fighting about this problem.
Today we settle it once and for all. We'll go through three levels, from easy to the problem that even adults get wrong. Solve along at every level!
Level one: Multiplication before addition.
What is three plus four times two? Many people just go left to right: three plus four is seven, times two is fourteen. Sadly, that's wrong.
The rule is: multiplication and division come before addition and subtraction. Times and divide are the strong operations. Plus and minus are the weak ones.
So first four times two, that's eight. Then three plus eight. Result: eleven.
Why does this rule exist? Imagine you buy one pen for one dollar and three notebooks for two dollars each. That's one plus three times two.
Of course you work out the notebooks first: three times two is six dollars. Plus the pen: seven dollars. The rule matches real life.
Mini quiz! What is ten minus two times three? Think for a second.
First two times three equals six. Then ten minus six. Result: four. Not twenty-four!
Pro tip: before you start, circle every multiplication and division. Then you instantly see what comes first.
Level two: Parentheses and exponents.
Parentheses beat everything. Whatever is inside the parentheses always gets calculated first.
Three plus four in parentheses, times two. Now the parentheses come first: seven. Then times two: fourteen. With parentheses you get a completely different answer.
Exponents come even before multiplication. Two plus three squared is two plus nine, so eleven. Not five squared!
The full order is: parentheses, exponents, multiplication and division, addition and subtraction. In the US you remember it as PEMDAS. In the UK it's BODMAS.
An example with everything: twenty minus, open parentheses, two plus one, close parentheses, times two squared.
First the parentheses: three. Then the exponent: two squared is four. Then multiply: three times four is twelve. Finally subtract: twenty minus twelve. Result: eight.
Mini quiz! What is five minus three in parentheses, cubed, plus one?
Parentheses: two. Exponent: two cubed is eight. Plus one: nine!
Level three: The PEMDAS trap.
PEMDAS has M before D. So does multiplication always come before division? Let's test it: eight divided by two times two.
If you do the multiplication first, you get two times two equals four, and eight divided by four equals two. That's wrong!
Multiplication and division are equally strong. Then the rule is always: left to right. Eight divided by two is four, times two is eight.

Same with addition and subtraction: ten minus three plus two. From the left: ten minus three is seven, plus two is nine. Not five!
Pro tip: think of division as a fraction. Eight divided by two times two is eight over two, times two. Then you instantly see: eight.
The finale: The internet problem.
Six divided by two, times one plus two in parentheses. First the parentheses: one plus two is three.
Now we have: six divided by two times three. Only multiplication and division, so left to right.
Six divided by two is three. Three times three is nine. By the standard rule, the answer is nine.
So why do so many people say one? Because they see two times the parentheses as one block and calculate two times three first. Then they get six divided by six, which is one.
Honestly, the problem is written in a confusing way on purpose. Some calculators and textbooks treat multiplication without a sign as stronger. That's exactly why people argue.
Mathematicians would never write it like this. They use a fraction bar or more parentheses. Then it's instantly clear what is meant.
By the rule you learn in school, the answer is nine. And now you can explain to anyone why.
The four most common mistakes.
Mistake one: just going left to right. Two plus three times four is fourteen, not twenty.
Mistake two: forgetting the exponent. Two times three squared is two times nine, so eighteen, not thirty-six.
Mistake three: always doing multiplication before division. Twelve divided by three times two is eight, not two.
Mistake four: missing the minus in front of parentheses. Ten minus, in parentheses, three plus two, is five, not nine.
